title: Orientation: an interface record
statement:
Work in the six-functor setting of [def-sf-datum]: finite-type schemes over the fixed algebraic closure $k$ of a finite field of characteristic $p$, with $\ell\ne p$, and coefficient stages $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Use its constructible finite-Tor categories, coefficient comparison data, derived operations, and structure morphisms $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. For every scheme $S$ in this setting, let $\Lambda_S$ be its coefficient object; Tate twists and shifts use the conventions of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and [def-sf-datum], so $K(m)=K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_S}\Lambda_S(m)$ for $K$ on $S$. In particular the integral coefficient object is the completed one and the algebraically closed coefficient stage is interpreted at a common finite extension.

For a smooth separated finite-type morphism $f:X\to Y$ of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$, an *orientation* is the component at $(f,\Lambda)$ of an orientation datum [def-sf-orientation]. Its isomorphism in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ is
$$
\gamma_{f,\Lambda_Y}:Lf^*\Lambda_Y(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^!\Lambda_Y.
$$
The family is natural in the base $Y$ and compatible with composition of smooth morphisms, etale base change, finite reduction, scalar extension and the pro-etale realization, in the sense of [def-sf-orientation], using the comparison maps of [def-sf-datum] at their defined coefficient stages. On the affine-line projection it is the canonical orientation specified in [def-sf-orientation]. Thus the compatibility conditions are conditions on the whole family, not on an isolated isomorphism for one $f$. For $f=a_X$, with $X$ smooth separated of pure dimension $d$ over $k$, the same isomorphism, read in the reverse direction and with $\omega_{X,\Lambda}=Ra_X^!\Lambda$ as in [def-sf-datum], reads
$$
\omega_{X,\Lambda}\cong\Lambda_X(d)[2d].
$$

For the concrete system, existence of this canonical family is a theorem, not an extra assumption of the six-functor interface. The source's construction pointers are finite smooth purity [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity], the tensor and base-change statements [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness], and the remaining coefficient stages [sk-thm-purity-transport]. These are forward pointers to the verification of the interface, not prerequisites for defining orientation data.

split_report.summary: One-level definition split with no new nodes: reused def-sf-datum for the operation/coefficient/dualizing setting, def-coefficient-twists-detailed for actual Tate objects, and def-sf-orientation for the coherent family. Restored the ambient hypotheses and affine-line normalization explicit in the detailed source, distinguished family compatibilities from one isolated isomorphism, and retained purity existence as forward construction pointers using current DAG ids rather than the absent sk-thm-smooth-purity and sk-prop-cohsm ids. The source existence pointer is not a definitional prerequisite. No exact full project attachment or Mathlib match: the Lean Orientation is finite-coefficient and individual-morphism only; separate finite-coefficient predicates do not supply the entire multistage constructed family.
